meaning: exclamatory sentence-ending particle (expressing arrival or completion)
conceptZh: 戴著格紋獵鹿帽的豬探長舉著超大放大鏡全速衝向神祕積木門，卻一頭撞扁在門上，震落的方框與彩漆木條剛好拼成「啦」字，他搖晃著揮手呼應「來啦」。
object: stout cartoon detective pig with an oversized magnifying glass and a tall wooden clue-door built from painted timber beams
morph: A square wooden door window and colorful painted timber beams shaken loose by the detective pig's headlong crash tumble and lock cleanly into the left mouth radical 口, center hand radical 扌, and right standing component 立 of the Traditional Chinese character 啦.
creativeAngle: 運用「衝刺撞擊（Charge and Crash）」喜劇節奏，讓急性子的豬探長為了追查門後線索全速衝撞積木大門，撞擊震落的門框與門栓自然組合成「啦」的口、扌、立三部件，並在結尾破門探頭做出「來啦」的趣味呼應，避免靜態變形並強化語音與畫面的連結。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D stylized cartoon animation set on a warm, sunlit cream-colored studio stage with soft pastel floor tiles and a clean, uncluttered background. 

0.0s–1.8s (Spot the Goal & First Attempt): On the far left, a stout cartoon detective pig in a tan trench coat and checked deerstalker hat peers through a comically oversized brass magnifying glass. Far across the stage on the right stands a tall wooden clue-door built from bright cobalt-blue painted timber beams with a square window frame and a golden paw-print clue sticker on it. Eager to inspect the clue, the detective pig lunges forward, trips over the heavy rim of his own giant magnifying glass, and skids on his snout in a silly false start as a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin speaks the first syllable slowly and distinctly: "啦 (˙ㄌㄚ)".

1.8s–3.5s (The Big Wind-Up & Charge): Popping back up determinedly, the detective pig hoists the giant magnifying glass like a battering ram, digs his little trotters hard into the floor, and leans way back in an exaggerated cartoon wind-up. With a puff of dust, he charges left-to-right across the frame at full tilt, ears flapping horizontally behind his hat.

3.5s–5.0s (The Squashy Crash & Glyph Assembly): He slams nose-first into the tall wooden door with a playful, cushioned cartoon BONK, squashing flat like a pancake against the panels before peeling off in a wobbly accordion bounce. The impact shakes the door apart, and its bright cobalt-blue painted beams tumble and lock cleanly in the center of the frame into the exact Traditional Chinese character "啦" just as the off-screen voice speaks the second syllable: "啦 (˙ㄌㄚ)" — the square window frame lands on the left as the mouth radical (口), three notched latch timbers snap into the middle hand radical (扌), and five sturdy door beams stack on the right as the standing radical (立).

5.0s–8.0s (Final Hold & "來啦" Payoff): For the final three full seconds, the saturated cobalt-blue glyph "啦" holds completely still, sharp, centered, and uncropped against the light cream background, filling about 70% of the frame height with generous margins. Down in the lower-left corner well clear of the strokes, the flattened detective pig pops back into shape with a dizzy, toothy grin, tips his crooked deerstalker hat, and waves both trotters forward in an enthusiastic "I'm here!" gesture right as the off-screen voice clearly pronounces the word: "來啦 (ㄌㄞˊ ˙ㄌㄚ)". The voice reads the full sequence "啦、啦、來啦 (˙ㄌㄚ、˙ㄌㄚ、ㄌㄞˊ ˙ㄌㄚ)" clearly and stops, accompanied only by soft cartoonish wooden bonk and spring sound effects, with no subtitles, vocabulary text, or watermarks on screen.
